account:
Today I have been keeping my appointments: inspecting grain at the mill, reviewing council correspondence, and visiting the neighbour for tea. I am now leaving the cottage for my sixteen-thirty office appointment. The mill chest held seventy-four hay bales this morning. The baker later told me the bread stall had eighty loaves at one emerald each. These are stock observations and reports, not proof that every household can afford or reach bread.

The unusual news is a recurring, vague rumour of a bridge or port change discussed at the bakery. Townsfolk named the baker, builder, freight operator and innkeeper as present. I have not established what was proposed, whether anything was agreed, or what its purpose would be. The baker could not reliably recall a specific proposal or agreement and said the bridge was passable this morning. The baker also reported that the innkeeper knew of no verified obstruction and suggested asking the builder or freight operator. The neighbour has heard no confirmed details either. I therefore regard this as an unresolved report, not an actual crossing change. The baker's direct concern was matching baking to demand and finding out whether households struggle to buy bread or reach the stall; no particular affected households were identified to me.

Town administration also has gaps: no council letters were delivered for today's review, and the custodian of the financial records remains unidentified despite our request for accounts. The secretary is receiving correspondence and expects my return. At eighteen hundred I have a confirmed appointment in the great hall concerning the innkeeper's community hospitality matter, with the secretary to remind and escort me. I know no further details of that matter and should not assume it is connected with the bakery rumours.
